page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 9354P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It delivers 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a dedicated allocation operating at a base frequency of 3.25 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 960 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in several categories. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Passmark memory scores rank in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and Geekbench multi-core scores consistently place in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier results in LLM inference prompt processing for small models and text generation for medium 7B models. Single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, perform in the middle 50%.

From a resource density perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and compute-heavy workloads due to its DDR5 memory architecture and dedicated AMD EPYC cores. The lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but the high memory-to-core ratio and strong memory bandwidth make it highly suitable for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
